subject: general
question: A dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price, but uses 900 gm weight for a kilogram. Find his profit per cent.
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = Cost price,

Using 900gm in place of 1000gm

**Formula used:**

% Profit = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/(Cost Price)×100

**Calculation:**

Let the price of 1gm of the product be '**x**'

then, the selling price** **of 1kg(1000gm) of the product will be **1000x**

as mentioned in the question that he is using 900gm of weight in place of 1000gm weight which means that the amount of product he will be selling is 900gm 

⇒The** C.P.** of the product will be 900x

By using the formula of profit percentage,

% profit = (1000x-900x)/(900x)× 100

% profit = (100x)/(900x)× 100

% profit = (100)/(9) \% = 11(1)/(9)\%

**∴ The dealer will be getting a profit of 11(1)/(9)\% .**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Calculation:

Since shopkeeper sells their goods on their C.P

He uses false weight. So,

C.P : S.P = 900 : 1000 = 9 : 10 

So, the profit % = (1/9) × 100 = 11(1)/(9)~\%~

**∴ The correct answer is 11(1)/(9)~\%~.**
